description: Hanabishi Miki (Hayate the Combat Butler) as a drawing reference: a 1.51 m anime schoolgirl (5.9 heads) in a relaxed A-pose, standing at the origin on the ground (z = 0) and facing -Y (her left hand on +X). 18 mesh objects, each a spatially compact group of parts (headband, hair, head, eyes, scarf, sidelocks, blouse, collar, back_hair, arm_l, face_marks, arm_r, legs, socks, skirt, shoes, ring, neck) so hidden-line removal stays fast; each object's display_color (its dominant material) colours it in the web UI's 3D views and is ignored by the drawing; per-part colours are the materials in examples/meshes/miki.obj/.mtl/.glb. Smooth groups turn the designed lines (bang cut, headband, collar, cuffs, hems) into feature edges and leave the rest to silhouettes. In the web UI choose it from the Example menu, orbit the board around her (the front button looks along +y at her face) and untick the 'labels' layer: every mesh vertex is labelled. The observer pane's sight rays (on by default) are drawn for every vertex of the first object, the headband, to show its perspective; untick them to see the whole figure. The default layers are the line drawing and the ground shadow (objects, cast_shadow); tick 'form_shadow' in the web UI for the shading fills (they are not hidden-line occluded, so back-lit hair shows through). The cast shadow is drawn per object (a translucent fill and outline for each), so where objects overlap (the head, hair, headband and face parts; arms over the skirt) the fills stack darker and inner outlines show; trace its outer silhouette. It is also not occluded by her legs and shoes. CLI: 'castplane render examples/miki.json -o out'. This scene JSON is the renderable form; the OBJ / GLB files are for other 3D software (a castplane import of them carries MESH_* warnings and renders slowly). Generated by tools/make_miki_model.py.
